You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Final answer format. First list the passages you rely on, copied VERBATIM from the files (no
  paraphrase, no ellipsis inside the quotation marks), then write the answer using only them:
  <evidence>
  [E1] "exact text" (file)
  [E2] "exact text" (file)
  </evidence>
  <answer>
  Your answer to the user. End every factual sentence with the evidence it rests on, e.g. [E1] or
  [E1, E2]. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no marker.
  </answer>
- The user sees only the <answer> part, so it must be complete and readable on its own.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

<evidence>
[E1] "When a meter seal has been broken by someone other than SRP’s personnel, SRP may assess a reconnection fee to the Customer’s billing." (doc.txt, lines 50-51)
[E2] "If SRP has evidence that any Customer has caused or allowed any of the conditions of Section 4.14.1 to exist, SRP may, at any time, without notice, discontinue the supply of electricity to the Customer and remove the meter or meters, apparatus, wires, and Service Lateral, as well as any evidence of the condition." (doc.txt, lines 61-65)
[E3] "SRP will charge the Customer for periods of unmetered service, estimated using data from available records and information. In the event of damage to meters or Service Equipment, the current Customer of record shall pay SRP based on estimated Energy usage not previously billed as well as any SRP costs associated with restoring proper metering or service." (doc.txt, lines 66-70)
[E4] "If SRP disconnects service to the Customer because of a violation of these Rules and Regulations, SRP will not restore service to the Customer until all amounts due SRP have been paid. SRP will include the full cost or expense incurred by SRP for the removal and reinstallation of the meter or meters, apparatus, wires, and Service Lateral. The Customer’s service entrance must comply with SRP’s then-current Electric Service Specifications before it can be re-energized." (doc.txt, lines 75-81)
</evidence>
<answer>
According to doc.txt, if a customer's meter seal was broken (by someone other than SRP's personnel) and SRP disconnected service, the customer must do the following to get service reconnected:

1. Pay all amounts due to SRP. SRP will not restore service until all amounts due have been paid [E4]. These amounts include:
   - The full cost or expense incurred by SRP for the removal and reinstallation of the meter or meters, apparatus, wires, and Service Lateral [E4].
   - Charges for periods of unmetered service, estimated using data from available records and information; if meters or Service Equipment were damaged, the current Customer of record must pay based on estimated energy usage not previously billed plus any SRP costs associated with restoring proper metering or service [E3].
   - A reconnection fee, which SRP may assess to the Customer's billing when a meter seal has been broken by someone other than SRP's personnel [E1].

2. Ensure the Customer's service entrance complies with SRP's then-current Electric Service Specifications before it can be re-energized [E4].

The document does not describe any additional application or procedural steps beyond paying all amounts due and bringing the service entrance into compliance with the Electric Service Specifications.
</answer>
